A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffuGPT/DiffuLLaMA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; v2 retains the original study and expands its supplementary evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model training, benchmark evaluations, adaptation ablations, generation examples, and inference-speed measurements in Sections 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds countdown reasoning, controlled AR comparisons, a self-correction case study, and additional diagnostic results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.4 and Algorithms 1-2 retain the diffusion objective, attention-mask annealing, shift operation, time-embedding-free architecture, and sampling procedure. The CodeLLaMA and countdown experiments apply the existing approach without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on countdown CD4, a constrained arithmetic-planning task (Appendix C.3, Table 7). Existing training corpora and QA, commonsense, mathematics, and infilling benchmarks remain. The added CodeLLaMA experiment reuses Starcoder and HumanEval infilling.

E2.justification: v2 adds substantially stronger controls: continued-pretrained GPT2-M in Table 9 and CodeLLaMA trained with FIM-SPM and FIM-PSM in Table 8. Its new CD4 comparison includes GPT2-scratch, LLaMA FT, and SoS. The original main-table comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include training AR and diffusion CodeLLaMA on 100M Starcoder tokens, testing two AR infilling formats, and continuing GPT2 pretraining on the same corpus and settings as DiffuGPT. Table 11 additionally compares T=8 with T=32. These add substantial controls and settings; the original protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially expands diagnostic evidence through a self-correction trajectory, infilling-format comparisons, an AR continued-pretraining control, and timestep sensitivity. Table 5 extends existing GSM8K ablations with newly reported ELBO losses alongside previously reported accuracies; removing shift or annealing was already tested in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing three-candidate self-consistency evaluation and 64-sample unconditional-generation setup are retained; no new statistical reporting practice appears.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores, latency measurements, and generation examples are retained, but substantial results are added. These include CD4 accuracy of 87.5 for DiffuGPT, new ELBO losses and continued-pretraining scores, and HumanEval pass@1 of 0.76 for Diffu-CodeLLaMA versus 0.80 for FIM-SPM and 0.74 for FIM-PSM. Table 11 adds T=8 results, including HellaSwag 47.1 alongside the retained T=32 score of 58.7.

T1.justification: The diffusion definitions, transition distributions, AR-objective connection, and ELBO derivations in Sections 2-3 and Appendix A remain unchanged, including Equations 1-25. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the central claims: adapting 127M-7B AR models using fewer than 200B tokens, outperforming earlier DLMs, competitive AR performance, and infilling/in-context-learning capabilities. Replacing some references to 'scaling' with 'adapting' or 'training' does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 now identifies stronger base AR models as a possible explanation for improvements with model size. Appendix B.1 explains corpus selection through distribution continuity. New appendix discussions interpret continued-pretraining results through stability gaps and limited new knowledge, and discuss infilling-format sensitivity and reduced-step accuracy tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies lm-evaluation-harness as the implementation basis and documents the added CodeLLaMA experiment's 100M-token budget and SPM/PSM formats. Core optimizer, tokenizer, hardware, training-budget, and code-access information remains unchanged; the new experiments receive relatively limited implementation detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds relevant references on attention-mask curricula, continual-pretraining stability, countdown reasoning, and evaluation tooling. The introduction newly acknowledges earlier LLaMA-to-DLM adaptation attempts by Ye et al. (2023), although Section 5 retains its statement that AR-to-diffusion adaptation remains unexplored. Most bibliography changes merely update formatting or publication details.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. v2 makes localized terminology and paragraph revisions, expands dataset explanations, adds appendix subsections on DLM advantages and AR continued pretraining, and updates author information, acknowledgments, and conference headers.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the appendix displays with ELBO, countdown, infilling-control, continued-pretraining, and timestep tables plus a color-marked self-correction trajectory. Existing figures remain, while the latency table moves from Table 5 to 10 and generation examples from Tables 6-8 to 12-14. Table 2 also gains clearer row grouping.

improvement.justification: The new continued-pretraining and FIM-trained AR controls partially address comparison weaknesses in v1, while the diagnostic analyses strengthen empirical support. The gains are limited by sparse documentation of the added experiments and selective interpretation: Table 8's diffusion score of 0.76 beats FIM-PSM at 0.74 but trails FIM-SPM at 0.80. Overall, v2 provides useful additional validation without fully resolving the broader comparison limitations.
